files: src/kernel/fat16.c: fat16_stamp_entry() encodes the kernel REALTIME clock (hb_clock_realtime_ms, kernel/time.c) into FAT16 date/time on create (fat16_open), mkdir, write/appends (fat16_write), O_TRUNC (fat16_truncate), ftruncate (fat16_truncate_to); fat16_entry_epoch() decodes back to epoch

in_os_tools_notes: pattern rules are unusable in-OS (FAT uppercase short names): synthetic Makefiles use EXPLICIT rules
SHELL must be set (make default /bin/sh does not exist on the boot disk): SHELL := /SH.BIN
in-OS TOUCH.BIN only creates (open O_CREAT, no utimens): it never moves mtime; the rewrite trigger uses CP.BIN (truncate+write), which is the kernel's real mtime-updating path

caveats_documented.two_second_resolution: FAT16 timestamps have 2-second granularity; GNU make treats equal mtimes as up to date.  Writes inside the same 2 s bucket can produce equal mtimes, so make run immediately after a fast rebuild may consider a target current.  Acceptance probes sleep >= 3 s between build and re-check; document for any in-OS build scheduling.
caveats_documented.guest_vs_host_date: guest RTC is UTC; host mtools staging writes local time.  Same calendar date in acceptance runs.
caveats_documented.no_rtc_machines: stamps fall back to the 1980 sentinel (valid FAT fields) when no RTC; unit tests fail loudly (year>=2026) rather than hang.
